title: Soft reservation lanes and proactive noise throttling for dedicated GPU tiers
creator: Diego Morales
description: Introduce a soft-reservation and proactive noise-throttling subsystem for Dedicated GPU pools to provide throughput guarantees while improving overall utilization. This ticket implements: (1) per-tenant soft reservations (time-windowed credits that bias scheduler decisions rather than hard slice GPUs), (2) a streaming noise detector that uses service-level signals (latency tails, KV cache churn, and per-request GPU memory spikes) to flag noisy tenants, and (3) an adaptive throttling controller that reduces allotment for noisy tenants and reclaims capacity into a shared burst pool. Goal: concrete SLO improvements for P95 latency and predictable per-tenant throughput while keeping fleet utilization >70%.
acceptance_criteria: Soft reservation API available in Dedicated tenant config and accepted by scheduler
Noise detector reaches >=85% precision on synthetic noisy neighbor scenarios in staging
Controller enforces throttles with max 3% false positive eviction rate during 24h soak in canary cluster
Per-tenant P95 latency meets configured SLO for 95% of tenants during 30-minute synthetic load tests
Automated rollback path and metrics dashboards instrumented in Console for rollout
implementation_notes: Scheduler change: add 'soft_reservation_weight' that increases slot scoring for a tenant during its active window
Reservation semantics: credits accrue over time and can be banked up to 3x nominal throughput for short bursts
Noise detector: sampled telemetry from runtime (token service latency, KV cache miss rate, ephemeral memory pressure) aggregated into a per-tenant noise score
Throttling controller: PID-style smoothing to avoid oscillation; initial limits bounded by tenant SLA and manual guardrails
Fallback: when a tenant is misclassified, eviction is limited to background best-effort buckets and we use immediate rollback flags via runtime control-plane
benchmarks: Staging run 2025-02-26: simulated 200 tenants with 10 noisy; noise detector precision=0.88, recall=0.72
Soak 48h 2025-03-01: fleet utilization improved from 62% -> 71% with soft reservations enabled
Latency tail improvement: median P95 for reserved tenants from 420ms -> 310ms under mixed load
open_issues: Edge case where two high-credit tenants saturate same GPU PU causing cross-tenant accelerator contention remains to be mitigated (proposed: affinity-aware bucketing)
Integration with Dedicated Autoscaler to honor soft reservations during scale-down requires API extension
Need a migration plan for customers currently using hard-slicing (Dedicated v1) to avoid surprise head-of-line blocking
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1132 - scheduler scoring and soft reservation model
https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/482 - dashboard panels for noise score and throttle actions
test_plan: Unit tests for scheduler scoring and reservation accounting
Integration test: synthetic noisy tenant generator + end-to-end throttle enforcement in staging
Chaos test: kill GPU driver on canary nodes and validate safe rollback path
Performance regression job comparing baseline runtime-1.18 vs feature branch over 24h
rollout_plan: Canary rollout over dedicated-us-west-2 cluster: week 1 enable noise detection read-only; week 2 enable soft reservations with conservative weights for 10% of tenants; week 3 enable adaptive throttling with human-in-loop alerts; full rollout after 2-week soak and SRE signoff. Rollback via feature flag to restore previous scheduler scoring and drain throttle actions.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: tenant_noise_score (gauge) with alert if >0.75 for 5m AND sustained request error increase
Throttle actions emitted as structured events with tenant_id, reason, duration
SLO dashboards: per-tenant P95, throughput, and throttle_count per minute
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives throttle healthy tenants -> Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds and undo window where throttled tenants get expedited credit recovery
Risk: attackers could try to game score by alternating patterns -> Mitigation: include long-window features (KV churn) and require sustained signal to trigger throttles
Risk: interactions with Dedicated autoscaler causing over-provisioning -> Mitigation: autoscaler integration work to consider soft_reservation_weight when deciding scale-down
decision_log: 2025-02-18: decided to use soft reservations (+weighting) rather than hard GPU slices to preserve utilization and offer burstability (owners: Lena Park, Marcus Chen)
2025-02-25: selected PID-inspired smoothing for throttle controller after spike oscillation experiment
2025-03-03: deferred encryption-of-saved-reservation-blob to next cycle due to low immediate risk and scope constraints
review_feedback: PM (Aparna Shah): add clearer customer migration notes and billing implications for reserved credits
Security (Rohit Patel): recommend threat model for score poisoning, accepted and added long-window features to detector
SRE (Maya Green): require automatic backoff to avoid throttling during controller flapping; implemented exponential backoff
